concerns.text: T015 defines 'Primary Baseline (Non-COVID Group)' as 'ALL other vaccines' but simultaneously creates a 'Non-COVID, Non-Flu' subset. The spec (FR-007) and plan (Phase 1) mandate the main analysis use the 'Non-COVID, Non-Flu' baseline to minimize confounding, while reserving the 'Non-COVID' (all other) group ONLY for sensitivity analysis. T015 conflates these, risking the main analysis using the wrong baseline.

T027 implements sensitivity analysis comparing 'Non-COVID (all other vaccines)' vs 'Flu-only'. The spec (FR-007) and plan (Phase 3.2) explicitly require comparing the 'Non-COVID, Non-Flu' baseline against the 'Flu-only' baseline. This task implements the wrong comparison logic, violating the constitutional requirement for confounding minimization.

T039 and T040 enforce a 5 GB memory limit for data cleaning. The spec (FR-006) and plan (Summary) define a single global constraint of '< 7 GB RAM'. Introducing an arbitrary 5 GB internal threshold without spec authorization constitutes a silent relaxation of the global constraint (by making it stricter than allowed) or a potential violation of the 'MVP' scope if the 5GB limit causes premature halts not anticipated by the 7GB spec.

T055 requires the report to include a 'Background Rate Unknown' disclaimer. The project notes explicitly state 'T024b has been removed as the 'Background Rate Unknown' flagging is inconsistent with the ROR/PRR/IC methodology'. The task re-introduces a requirement that was explicitly rejected in the planning phase, creating a contradiction between the task and the project's own re-planning decisions.

T027 and T028 depend on 'top 5 signals' identified from T026. However, T026 is marked as 'rejected/missing' in the current state. The task list assumes the existence of an artifact (signals.csv) that is currently non-existent, creating a circular dependency where the sensitivity analysis cannot be implemented until the signal detection is fixed, yet the task list treats them as parallel or sequential without acknowledging the block.
